_comment_feedback_encoding: Driver feedback is signed: negative = understeer, positive = oversteer; |2..3| clearly felt, |4..5| approaching undrivable / undrivable. Every rule's verdict <-> feedback_sign pair must match VERDICT_EXPECTED_FEEDBACK_SIGN (understeer -> negative, oversteer -> positive, unstable_yaw none). The consistency-gate override uses the same map.
_comment_parameters: suggestion.parameter = setup_parameters.json registry key. suggestion is one action or a list (atomic package, or an axle pair FL+FR / RL+RR -- no axle-level registry key). Action = {parameter, direction, delta} (signed, native unit; feasible if current + delta within value_space) or {parameter, target} (categorical, e.g. abs_position; always feasible). weight sits at rule level.
_comment_trigger: condition.trigger. 'data': fires from classify_fn (verdict + min_severity) on the rule's phases; feedback only modulates the score (agreement_bonus / conflict_penalty / 1.0). 'driver': fires from feedback_sign/min_feedback_abs alone (score ~ max |feedback|/5); condition.verdict is only the agreement reference, never a gate. 'both': data AND driver condition must both hold; no further modulation, higher weight.
_comment_source_balance: source_balance (0..1): multiplier after agreement/conflict -- data rules x (1 - sb) * 2, driver rules x sb * 2, 'both' always 1.0. 0.5 = neutral. At the extremes a rule still evaluates but scores 0 and drops at min_score_to_show. Weighs who may raise a hypothesis; agreement/conflict weighs what the other source says.
_comment_worst_corner: worst_corner_multiplier: applied once to every match on a corner the driver flagged 'worst', after source_balance and agreement/conflict, any trigger. Default 1.5; unflagged corners x1.0; several flagged corners each get it.
_comment_cell_id_status: cell_id = key into the engineer decision matrix (kept outside the repo); one entry per cell, including no-action cells (OS-BRK-low, INST-ENT) and escalations. status: elicited (from the matrix, not yet reviewed in-tool), reviewed, held (escalation, specified but never fires -- no history of applied changes yet), dropped (cell defines no action), retired (superseded). held/dropped/retired never fire.
_comment_severity_floor_repair: The four held CS-only understeer escalations (US-BRK-low/med/high-esc, US-APX-med-esc) use min_severity 'moderate': 'strong' needs strong CS AND destabilising yaw on the same phase slice, unreachable for a CS-only escalation. Proportionality comes from action_class and the provenance caps instead.
_comment_consistency_gate: No recommendation unless the verdict repeats across laps at the same stable_corner_id. Checked per lap for data/both rules: min_repeat_laps (absolute) AND min_repeat_fraction (of the corner's analysed laps). Driver rules exempt (feedback has no lap dimension).
_comment_consistency_gate_feedback_overr: Override: one matching lap passes the gate (skips both laps floor and fraction) when raw |feedback| >= feedback_override_raw_min AND scaled |feedback| >= feedback_override_scaled_min (scaled = raw x driver_level_weighting). Raw 4 = approaching undrivable. The separate scaled floor stops a low-level driver's complaint piercing the gate (raw 4 x 0.6 = 2.4 < 4.0). Direction must match the rule's verdict. A near-undrivable complaint on a corner already moderate+ in the data counts as repeat evidence.
_comment_escalation_enabled: Undrivable-feedback tier, same raw_min/scaled_min pair (|4| is one boundary, not two). At |raw| >= raw_min a corner never shows silent emptiness. Evidence is lap-level (an aggregate can dilute a 2-of-4-lap pattern to normal), any phase the feedback direction could cover. Outcomes: rule with matching lap evidence + scaled floor -> forced recommended, URGENT, caps bypassed (re-fired with that lap's data if the aggregate never matched); opposite-direction evidence only -> urgent contradiction row; no evidence -> 'no elicited rule covers this case' row. |5| = driver close to crashing -> must always reach the engineer. false = tier off (gate override unaffected).
_comment_change_budget: Not the display cap (max_recommendations, up to 8 shown). Marks the top default_max non-conflicted, feasible results as 'selected' after ranking, skipping conflicted/infeasible ones. absolute_cap reserved for a manual override; never auto-selects past default_max.
_comment_action_class: Data-trigger match at moderate severity without driver corroboration on the same phases = ADVISORY (observation + likely lever, never budget-eligible). Mild understeer is this car's stable baseline. RECOMMENDED if trigger in always_recommended_triggers, or data trigger with severity in data_trigger_recommended_severities (default strong) or corroborated. Bucket RECOMMENDED if any match qualifies.
_comment_driver_level_weighting: Driver.driving_level (1-10) -> feedback_weight, applied once where fb_value is computed: scales driver-trigger scores and the data/both corroboration check. neutral_level 5 = unweighted; default_weight for None / not in table. A low level can stop a borderline driver rule from firing at all -- intended. Table values elicited, not data-derived.

rules.name: Entry understeer (data) -> soften front ARB
rules.rationale: Softens the front ARB to reduce front lateral load transfer and free up grip on the sliding front axle at turn-in.

rules.name: Exit oversteer / traction (data) -> soften rear ARB
rules.rationale: Softens the rear ARB to reduce rear lateral load transfer and restore traction and stability under power on exit.

rules.name: Apex understeer (data) -> soften front ARB
rules.rationale: Softens the front ARB to reduce front lateral load transfer and free up front grip through a sustained, high-load apex.

rules.name: Unstable yaw on entry (data) -> soften rear ARB
rules.rationale: Softens the rear ARB to free up rear grip and add yaw damping while trail-braking into the corner.

rules.name: Driver-reported exit oversteer (driver) -> soften rear ARB
rules.rationale: Softens the rear ARB to free up rear grip and address the driver's reported exit oversteer.

rules.name: Driver-reported entry understeer (driver) -> soften front ARB
rules.rationale: Softens the front ARB to free up front grip and address the driver's reported entry understeer.

rules.name: Entry understeer, data + driver agree (both) -> soften front ARB
rules.rationale: Data and driver agree on entry understeer: softening the front ARB frees up front grip at turn-in.

rules.name: Understeer, braking, low speed -> ABS front-stable map
rules.rationale: Add 0.5mm front toe-out to sharpen turn-in response and address front-axle understeer risk under braking at low speed. If that isn't enough, an ABS map change is the next lever (see the escalation note).

rules.name: Escalation: US-BRK-low -> ABS try-and-error, FA stability target
rules.rationale: If front toe-out alone doesn't resolve it, try 1-2 ABS positions toward the front-axle-stable map within the current dry grip bracket.

rules.name: Understeer, braking, medium speed -> front bump LS softer
rules.rationale: Open front low-speed bump damping 3 clicks (both corners) to soften nose-dive control and slow front-axle load transfer under trail-braking.

rules.name: Escalation: US-BRK-med -> front ARB softer, rear ARB stiffer
rules.rationale: If the damper change alone isn't enough, soften front ARB 2 positions and stiffen rear ARB 1 position to shift roll stiffness rearward and free up front-axle grip under trail-braking.

rules.name: Understeer, braking, high speed -> wing up + rake forward (package)
rules.rationale: One wing step up plus 1mm of forward rake (front ride height down, rear up) adds rear downforce and shifts the aero balance rearward, raising braking-phase stability so more front grip stays available. Applied together as one package.
rules.practice_note: ride_height_front is typically pinned at its lower limit by standing practice (author-elicited 2026-09-24); the rear action usually carries this package.

rules.name: Escalation: US-BRK-high -> front bump HS softer
rules.rationale: If the wing+rake package alone doesn't resolve it, open front high-speed bump damping 2 clicks for extra compliance.

rules.name: Understeer, turn-in, low speed -> front toe more toe-out
rules.rationale: Add 0.5mm front toe-out to sharpen initial turn-in response and counter front-axle understeer at low speed.

rules.name: Understeer, turn-in, medium speed -> diff position down
rules.rationale: Drop the differential one locking-torque position to let the front axle rotate more freely into the corner on turn-in trail-throttle.

rules.name: Understeer, turn-in, high speed -> wing down
rules.rationale: Drop the wing one step to reduce rear downforce and shift the aero balance toward more front grip at turn-in speed.

rules.name: Understeer, apex, low speed -> front ARB softer
rules.rationale: Soften the front ARB 1 position (both corners) to free up mid-corner front grip under sustained apex load. Alternative: stiffen the rear ARB 1 position instead, which rotates the car more and eases the same understeer.

rules.name: Understeer, apex, medium speed -> diff position down
rules.rationale: Drop the differential one locking-torque position to ease the understeer a locked diff can induce through the apex under partial throttle.

rules.name: Escalation: US-APX-med -> TC LAT up (power-understeer)
rules.rationale: If the diff change alone isn't enough, raise TC LAT one position -- cuts torque sooner under lateral load, keeping more reserve on the front axle. Only applies when throttle is involved (on-power understeer), not an off-throttle push.

rules.name: Understeer, apex, high speed -> front camber more negative
rules.rationale: Add 0.1deg more front negative camber (both corners) to add peak front grip under sustained high-speed apex load. Typical practice is a 0.2deg step (two clicks); check tyre wear pattern first, and consider a one-sided change if only one corner needs it.

rules.name: Understeer, exit, low speed -> TC LON down
rules.rationale: Drop TC LON one position to allow a touch more wheel spin, easing power-on understeer at low exit speed.

rules.name: Understeer, exit, medium speed -> rear ARB stiffer
rules.rationale: Stiffen the rear ARB 1 position (both corners) to rotate the car more on exit and counter the understeer.

rules.name: Understeer, exit, high speed -> rear ARB stiffer
rules.rationale: Same fix as medium-speed exit understeer: stiffen the rear ARB 1 position (both corners) to rotate the car more on exit.

rules.name: Oversteer, braking, low speed -> none
rules.rationale: No first-change action defined for this scenario; recorded for completeness, never fires.

rules.name: Oversteer, braking, medium speed -> rear ARB softer
rules.rationale: Soften the rear ARB 1 position to free up rear grip under brake-release yaw.

rules.name: Oversteer, braking, high speed -> rear ARB softer
rules.rationale: Same fix as medium-speed braking oversteer: soften the rear ARB 1 position to free up rear grip.

rules.name: Oversteer, turn-in, low speed -> front toe toward zero
rules.rationale: Reduce front toe-out by 0.5mm toward zero to calm the extra turn-in rotation toe-out adds, easing oversteer at low speed.

rules.name: Oversteer, turn-in, medium speed -> diff position up
rules.rationale: Add one differential locking-torque position to stabilise the rear axle on turn-in trail-throttle.

rules.name: Oversteer, turn-in, high speed -> wing up
rules.rationale: Add one wing step to add rear downforce and counter rear instability at turn-in speed.

rules.name: Oversteer, apex, low speed -> front ARB stiffer
rules.rationale: Under sustained apex load, two valid levers depending on which axle is closer to its limit: stiffen front ARB 1 position, or soften rear ARB 1 position instead. Engineer's call, not a fixed first change.

rules.name: Oversteer, apex, medium speed -> diff position up
rules.rationale: Under partial throttle, add one diff locking-torque position to stabilise the rear axle, or address it through toe/camber/ARB instead -- engineer's call.

rules.name: Oversteer, apex, high speed -> front camber less negative
rules.rationale: Under sustained high-speed apex load, three possible levers: a spring change, softening rear ARB 1 position, or 0.1deg less front negative camber -- engineer's call on which fits the car at the time.

rules.name: Oversteer, exit, low speed -> TC LON up
rules.rationale: Add one TC LON position to cut wheel spin and reduce power-on rear-axle oversteer.

rules.name: Oversteer, exit, medium speed -> rear ARB softer
rules.rationale: Soften the rear ARB 1 position to free up rear grip on power application.

rules.name: Oversteer, exit, high speed -> wing up
rules.rationale: Add one wing step to add rear downforce and stability on power application at high exit speed.

rules.name: Instability, braking, low speed -> ABS rear-stable map
rules.rationale: Try 1-2 ABS positions toward the rear-axle-stable map within the current dry grip bracket, to calm unstable yaw under braking at low speed.

rules.name: Instability, braking, medium speed -> rake reduction
rules.rationale: Reduce rake by 1mm (front ride height up, rear down) to shift the aero pressure centre forward and calm destabilising yaw while trail-braking.
rules.practice_note: ride_height_front is typically pinned at its lower limit by standing practice (author-elicited 2026-09-24); the rear action usually carries this package.

rules.name: Instability, braking, high speed -> front toe more toe-out
rules.rationale: Add 0.5mm front toe-out to sharpen the front axle's response to counter-steer input, adding authority against destabilising yaw while trail-braking.

rules.name: Instability, combined entry -> dropped
rules.rationale: No first-change action defined for combined entry instability; recorded for completeness, never fires.

_comment_elicitation_provenance: Provenance per matrix rule. engineer-verbatim: 12 cells + 2 held escalations inheriting it. project-default: 8 cells asterisked in the matrix (US-BRK-low, US-TIN-high, US-APX-low, US-APX-high, OS-BRK-high, OS-EXIT-med sign-corrected, INST-BRK-low, INST-BRK-high) + US-BRK-high-esc (defaulted direction). mirror-derived: 6 cells marked 'm' (OS-TIN-low/med/high, OS-APX-low/med/high), mirrored from the opposite verdict's lever. null for dropped/retired. Non-verbatim -> capped to ADVISORY (action_class.cap_non_verbatim_to_advisory) until the engineer confirms the cell and status becomes 'reviewed'.
